title: Approval gate bypassed via In-review status carrying severity/VEX downgrade
rationale: Root cause: `backend/application/core/services/assessment.py:75`. The `and new_status != Status.STATUS_IN_REVIEW` term was ANDed against the *entire* "something changed" group, so any request with `new_status == "In review"` short-circuited the whole NEEDS_APPROVAL branch to AUTO_APPROVED — even when severity, priority, or VEX were changed in the same call, and `_update_observation` then applied those changes unconditionally. The fix moves the IN_REVIEW exemption inside the status disjunct only. Now IN_REVIEW suppresses approval solely for the status field; a concurrent severity/priority/vex change still satisfies its own disjunct and forces NEEDS_APPROVAL. This enforces the recommendation: IN_REVIEW exempts approval only when status is the sole change.
variants_checked: Approval-gate logic is centralized in `assessment.py:save_assessment`; `_update_observation` and `assessment_approval` are downstream sinks with no independent gate. Call sites grepped: `observations_bulk_actions.py:observations_bulk_assessment` (lines 41, 94), `risk_acceptance_expiry_task.py` (line 18), `views_observation.py:assessment` (line 148) — all delegate to `save_assessment` and inherit the fix. No other site recomputes `assessment_status`, so a single-point fix covers all variants.
bypass_considered: Tried `{status: "In review", priority: <new>}` and `{status: "In review", vex_justification: <new>}` — the original `and new_status != IN_REVIEW` global term would have auto-approved both. After the fix, the priority disjunct `(log_priority and log_priority != current_priority)` and the vex disjunct remain true and are no longer suppressed by IN_REVIEW, so the expression evaluates to NEEDS_APPROVAL. The only remaining auto-approve path with IN_REVIEW is a status-only change (no severity/priority/vex delta), which is the intended exemption. No input variation reaches AUTO_APPROVED while downgrading severity/priority/vex.
test_note: No `test_assessment.py` exists under `backend/unittests/core/services/`. Add one there in the project's existing style (BaseTestCase + mock). The test should call `save_assessment` with `_get_assessments_need_approval` returning True and `_update_observation`/`create_observation_log` patched, passing `new_status=Status.STATUS_IN_REVIEW` together with `new_severity=Severity.SEVERITY_NONE` on an observation whose `current_severity` differs, then assert the `create_observation_log` call received `assessment_status=Assessment_Status.ASSESSMENT_STATUS_NEEDS_APPROVAL`. Before the fix this asserts AUTO_APPROVED (fails); after, NEEDS_APPROVAL (passes). A companion case with only `new_status=STATUS_IN_REVIEW` and no severity change should still assert AUTO_APPROVED to guard the intended exemption. I did not write the file to disk since the task is read-only/no-edit; the diff above is the load-bearing change.
review_reason: The single hunk relocates `new_status != Status.STATUS_IN_REVIEW` from gating the entire OR-group (original line 75) into the `log_status` disjunct alone (diff lines 10-14), fixing the root cause: previously any severity/priority/vex change rode along as AUTO_APPROVED whenever `new_status` was set to IN_REVIEW, bypassing `_get_assessments_need_approval` (assessment.py:67). The fix preserves the legitimate carve-out (a pure move-to-review needs no approval) while restoring approval for other field changes, adds no new attack surface, and is contained entirely within `save_assessment` at the cited location with no caller changes needed.
